Prompt students by asking questions to focus their thinking: 'How did the author include the sun and moon in this story? Why do you think the author included the sun and moon in this way?' 'What is this story mostly about? Why do you think the author chose to write this story?'
verdicts.rationale: The standard requires students to refer to parts of texts when supporting an idea, answer, or opinion. During Work Time C, students independently write and draw responses to the guiding question using the sentence frame "I think the author wrote about the ______ because __________," and teacher prompts direct them to think about how the author included the sun and moon and what the story is mostly about. This shows students forming text-based ideas. However, the lesson never explicitly asks students to point to, cite, or reference a specific part of the text (a page, sentence, illustration, or passage) to support their answer; the support is drawn from general recall of the read-aloud rather than from locating and referring to specific text evidence. Because the student performs a version of the act (supporting an idea with text-derived reasoning) but in a narrower form than the standard requires (no explicit reference to a specific part of the text), the clause is partially met.
